headline: A suspected Russian-speaking attacker turned hundreds of AI agents loose on PaperCut print servers and compromised 395 organizations in 48 countries, while Anthropic reported Russian criminals using Claude to automate malware evasion.

emerging_trends.text: Two separate crews put frontier models to work as labor this week: one aimed hundreds of AI agents at PaperCut print servers and broke into 395 organizations, and another used Claude to rewrite malware until detection engines stopped catching it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep hunting the software that everything else depends on, chaining two already-patched Artifactory flaws to seize administrator control and plant backdoors in the repository that feeds corporate build pipelines.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Intruders Backdoor Unpatched JFrog Artifactory Servers

emerging_trends.text: A vendor breach keeps paying the intruders weeks later, as the customer addresses taken from Trezor's email provider Brevo fed a phishing run that reached 347,000 people and hooked 2,500 of them.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Surfshark Test Server and Trezor Phishing Fallout

topics.title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign
topics.latest_developments: PaperCut released maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13, and 24.1.10 that replace every emergency patch the company had pushed for the two actively exploited flaws, and GreyNoise detailed the attacker's method: a private lab holding a vulnerable copy of PaperCut NG/MF and an Active Directory domain, where the suspected Russian-speaking operator built and tested the exploit before handing the break-ins to AI agents that reached at least 440 instances at 395 organizations in 48 countries.
topics.summary: PaperCut NG/MF runs print management for schools, universities, and enterprises worldwide, and the exploited pair chains an authentication bypass with remote code execution. Administrators should move straight to 26.0.5, 25.0.13, or 24.1.10 and hunt for unfamiliar accounts and outbound connections to 45.142.193.132.

sources.title: PaperCut Replaces Emergency Patches With Fixes for Two Actively Exploited Flaws
AI agents exploited PaperCut flaws to breach 395 organizations
PaperCut Flaws Exploited in AI-Powered Attacks
AI-powered attack exploited PaperCut flaws to hack 395 organizations

topics.title: Surfshark Test Server and Trezor Phishing Fallout
topics.latest_developments: Surfshark disclosed that a configuration error left one of its internal test servers facing the internet and hackers reached the engineering material, internal configurations, and proxy servers on it; Trezor put numbers on the phishing that followed the breach at its email provider Brevo, counting 347,000 addresses targeted and 2,500 customers who clicked the malicious link; and IDScan confirmed that hackers reached customer data in its cloud platform.
topics.summary: IDScan, the Louisiana identity verification firm that runs ID checks for car rental companies, retailers, and cannabis dispensaries, posted its acknowledgment on September 4, 2026 without naming a victim count, days after researchers tied it to a dark-web trove of 153 million driver's license scans. Trezor customers should treat any email asking for a recovery seed as theft in progress.

sources.title: Surfshark Systems Targeted by Hackers
Surfshark VPN says hackers breached internal testing, proxy servers
Trezor: 347,000 users targeted in phishing attacks after Brevo breach
IDScan confirms breach after 153 million driver's licenses leak on dark web

topics.title: Criminals Point Claude at Malware Evasion
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic reported that Russian hackers used Claude to automate malware evasion and that criminal groups increasingly attack AI vendors' own infrastructure, in one case stealing a pre-release Claude model; Microsoft's security researchers separately documented an AI-assisted business email compromise campaign that impersonates executives and sends fabricated invoices to push finance teams into ACH payment fraud.
topics.summary: Attackers now fold commercial models into ordinary criminal work, using them to mutate malware past detection engines and to write convincing executive impersonations, and they treat the model vendors themselves as targets worth breaching. Finance teams should confirm every payment-detail change through a channel separate from email.

sources.title: Anthropic Says Russian Hackers Used Claude AI to Automate Malware Evasion
Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud

topics.title: Intruders Backdoor Unpatched JFrog Artifactory Servers
topics.latest_developments: Wiz reported attacks running from August 15 through September 8, 2026 in which intruders chained two JFrog Artifactory flaws to take administrator control of self-hosted servers and plant backdoors, reaching only the servers whose operators had skipped JFrog's earlier fixes; CISA on September 10, 2026 added two MikroTik RouterOS bugs already under exploitation, CVE-2026-67277 and CVE-2026-86060, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: Artifactory holds the packages that software build pipelines pull from, so a backdoor there reaches every application a company ships. Operators of self-hosted Artifactory should apply JFrog's fixes, audit administrator accounts, and inspect stored artifacts for tampering.

sources.title: Attackers Chain JFrog Artifactory Flaws to Gain Admin Control and Plant Backdoors
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

topics.title: Conti Sentence and Treasury's Scam Reporting Push
topics.latest_developments: A Ukrainian national drew four years in prison for his role in Conti ransomware attacks during 2021 and 2022, and the U.S. Department of the Treasury urged banks to file more reports on cyber-enabled scams, tallying nearly $13 billion in losses since 2023 as scam compounds expand worldwide.
topics.summary: Treasury wants banks to feed it more detail on what happens to defrauded customers, the raw material for sanctions and seizures against the Southeast Asian and African compounds. Banks should route scam cases into suspicious activity reports rather than closing them as ordinary fraud.

sources.title: Conti ransomware gang member sentenced to 4 years in prison
Treasury urges banks to file cyber scam reports, noting nearly $13 billion in losses since 2023

topics.title: UNC3569 Rides Sogou Input Method to GRAYRABBIT
topics.latest_developments: Gen Digital published research on September 10, 2026 showing that the China-linked group UNC3569 exploited a flaw in Sogou Input Method, the Tencent-owned tool that ranks among the most widely used ways to type Chinese characters on Windows, starting each intrusion with a crafted link and finishing with a backdoor called GRAYRABBIT that carries the logged-in user's full rights.
topics.summary: Sogou Input Method sits on millions of Windows desktops and loads into every application that accepts typing, which makes it an unusually quiet foothold. Organizations with Chinese-language users should inventory Sogou installations and update them.

sources.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor

business_politics.title: Houthis Take the Bab al-Mandeb
business_politics.latest_developments: The Iran-backed Houthis captured an island and a coastal town, giving them effective control of the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint as of Friday, September 11, a step beyond the seizure of the Red Sea port of Mocha reported a day earlier.
business_politics.summary: Bab al-Mandeb carries traffic between the Gulf of Aden and the Suez Canal and serves as the main alternative for cargo that can no longer transit the Strait of Hormuz. The militants now hold ground on both approaches, and traders marked up the risk to Middle East crude exports even as oil slipped Friday after the prior session's surge.

sources.title: Iran-Backed Houthis Take Effective Control of Bab al-Mandeb Chokepoint
Oil Prices Slip After Recent Surge Amid Supply Risks

business_politics.title: Diesel Hits $6 and the IEA Writes Off Hormuz
business_politics.latest_developments: The International Energy Agency said Friday, September 11, that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen this year and cut its 2026 global oil demand outlook by 2.5 million barrels a day, hours after U.S. retail diesel set a record at $6 a gallon.
business_politics.summary: Crude trades above $100 a barrel and heads for a 10% weekly gain after the U.S.-Iran escalation and Houthi attacks on shipping and Saudi energy sites. Diesel prices set the pace for American farming, trucking, and industrial costs, and they land on households already squeezed on affordability, while Iran and the Gulf states prepare to meet on a temporary Iran-Oman shipping arrangement that regional governments hope opens a path to reopening the strait.

sources.title: IEA warns of ‘lost period’ in global oil demand
US diesel hits record $6 a gallon on Iran supply shock
U.S.-Iran Escalation to Delay Oil Flow Recovery Into Next Year, IEA Says
Iran and Gulf states to meet in push for Hormuz deal

business_politics.title: The Bond Rout Pauses Before the CPI
business_politics.latest_developments: U.S. and European government bond yields edged lower Friday morning, September 11, interrupting the global selloff hours before the August U.S. consumer-price report, as traders raised the odds that the Federal Reserve lifts rates at next week's meeting.
business_politics.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield sits just under 5%, the highest in nearly three years, after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's $6 billion buyback of 10- to 20-year paper failed to steady the market; investors call the operation far too small for the job. Gold heads for a weekly loss of more than 2%, the dollar firmed, and the climb in borrowing costs now threatens equities and the pace of the economy.

sources.title: Scott Bessent fails to break ‘fever’ in US bond market
Yields on U.S., European Government Bonds Lower But Still Near Multiyear Highs
Bond markets stabilise after global sell-off
Gold Set for Weekly Loss as Rate-Hike Expectations Pressure Prices

business.title: The North Shore Braces for a Season Without Baseball
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, September 11, on what a Major League Baseball work stoppage would cost the businesses around PNC Park if the Pirates play no games next season.
business.summary: Restaurants, bars, and parking operators on Pittsburgh's North Shore build their year around 81 Pirates home dates at PNC Park, and owners there now weigh staffing and revenue against the chance that the 2027 season never opens.

sources.title: If the Pirates don’t play next season, where does that leave the North Shore?

business.title: Ranking Pittsburgh's Rankings
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper's Affordable-ish Housing column on Friday, September 11, went through the ranked lists the city keeps landing on and graded the lists themselves.
business.summary: Pittsburgh turns up on national rankings for everything from best place to live without a car to best city for good neighbors, and the column weighs which of those lists carry any weight for people deciding where to rent or buy here.

sources.title: Affordable-ish Housing in Pittsburgh: Ranking the rankings edition

around_town.title: Flight 93 Marks 25 Years
around_town.latest_developments: The observance itself runs Friday, September 11, at the Flight 93 National Memorial near Shanksville, with President Trump attending a separate ceremony at the Pentagon.
around_town.summary: United Airlines Flight 93 came down in a field in Somerset County on September 11, 2001, after the 40 passengers and crew fought back, and families, first responders, and visitors gather at the memorial to read the names. WPXI spoke with Jack Grandcolas, who lost his wife and their unborn child on the flight and described how her actions guided his own recovery, and PublicSource collected readers' memories from across the region.

sources.title: Flight 93 Memorial ceremonies today mark 25 years since 9/11 attacks

9/11 memories vivid across Pittsburgh region

around_town.title: One Superintendent for Rochester and New Brighton
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Friday, September 11, on the single superintendent now running both the Rochester and New Brighton school districts in Beaver County.
around_town.summary: Two small Beaver County districts share one chief administrator, an arrangement that spreads a single salary across both payrolls and doubles the school boards, budgets, and buildings one person answers for.

sources.title: Two small school districts. One very busy boss.

around_town.title: Bradford Woods Sets a Meeting on Its Future
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Friday, September 11, that Bradford Woods will present the results of this year's community survey at a public meeting at 6 p.m. Thursday, October 1, at the Bradford Woods Volunteer Fire Company.
around_town.summary: The borough of Bradford Woods, in northern Allegheny County, surveyed residents earlier this year about what they want from the community and will use the October meeting to walk through the answers and take comment.

sources.title: Residents urged to help shape future of Bradford Woods

events.title: 'The Lion King' Opens the Broadway Season
events.latest_developments: TribLive reviewed "Disney's The Lion King" on Friday, September 11, calling it a majestic opening to the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust's 2026-27 PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series at the Benedum Center downtown.
events.summary: The show has grossed more than $2 billion in almost 30 years on Broadway, the highest total any Broadway musical has reached, and its puppetry and staging carry the visual weight that opens the Cultural Trust's season at the Benedum Center in Pittsburgh's Cultural District.

sources.title: Review: ‘Disney’s The Lion King’ is a majestic start to the PNC Broadway in Pittsburgh Series season at the Benedum

events.title: Sketch Lab Report Returns to Arcade Comedy
events.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper previewed the third volume of Sketch Lab Report on Friday, September 11.
events.summary: Sketch Lab Report at Arcade Comedy Theater downtown showcases new sketch writing from the theater's writing program, and City Paper describes this round as subversive and inventive humor built by local writers.

sources.title: Arcade Comedy Theater gets sketchy with writing showcase

events.title: Three Tours of Houses, Gardens, and a Campus
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette laid out three fall tours Friday, September 11, covering old houses and gardens in the Mexican War Streets on the North Side and in Shadyside, and the historic campus and church at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe.
events.summary: The Mexican War Streets and Shadyside tours open private houses and gardens to visitors, and the Saint Vincent College tour walks the Benedictine campus and its church in Unity Township, Westmoreland County.

sources.title: These 3 tours showcase old homes, gardens, a church and a historic campus

around_teams.title: Hiles Puts the Standard on McCarthy
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote Friday, September 11, that setting a new Steelers standard ranks as head coach Mike McCarthy's top priority in his first season.
around_teams.summary: McCarthy takes over a franchise that has gone years without a playoff win, and Hiles argues the measure of 2026 lies in the habits and expectations McCarthy installs rather than the win total, starting with Sunday's opener against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: Setting the new Steelers standard should be Mike McCarthy's top priority this season

around_teams.title: Rodgers Savors a Last Season
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Thursday, September 10, that quarterback Aaron Rodgers plans to savor what he calls a special season in Pittsburgh as his career winds down.
around_teams.summary: Rodgers, who opens his second year with the Steelers on Sunday, September 13, against the Atlanta Falcons, has told teammates and reporters he treats this run as the end of the line, and he spoke with the media at practice Wednesday, September 9, alongside DK Metcalf, Alex Highsmith, and Eli Heidenreich a day later.

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Runs the Week 1 Numbers
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Thursday's SNR Drive, September 10, on Steelers season what-ifs and Williamson's Week 1 statistical packet.
around_teams.summary: The Steelers-produced show also recapped the NFL's Wednesday night kickoff, went around the college slate, and brought on a Steelers beat writer ahead of Sunday's opener against the Atlanta Falcons.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: Superintelligence is a Fairy Tale. But Chasing It Can Still Cause Harm.
reading.summary: Newport answers Anthropic employees who said publicly that the systems they build could kill billions, arguing that superintelligence remains a story people tell themselves. He holds that the race toward it still does real damage, in the resources it consumes and the harms it creates along the way.

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: The iPhone Duo, The Intelligent Personal Hub, Apple Watch Audio Intelligence
reading.summary: Ben Thompson reads Apple's latest launch as another demonstration of what integrating hardware and software buys the company. He names Apple's belief in the primacy of apps as its largest blind spot in an AI era that favors an intelligent personal hub.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Concentration Risk
reading.summary: Zitron takes up the concentration of the market and the economy in a handful of AI companies. The piece extends his running case against the circular financing that runs among Nvidia, OpenAI, and the hyperscalers.
